title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-world-heavyweight-championship
label: Troy Tornado

won.source: Excessive Force, Sunday Week 4 June 2008 (in-game): 'Troy Tornado defeated Tommy Cornell', 'Suddenly, TCW has a new World Heavyweight Champion.'

how: Won from Tommy Cornell at Excessive Force, coming off a failed top-rope attack with the Star Maker, after Painful Procedure ringed the match to cut off Syndicate help; Edd Stone's missile dropkick from the Hangtime structure and a Savate Kick from Steve Gumble on Cornell came first. He keeps it through July 2008, beating Chris Rockwell and Wolf Hawkins in a three-way match at Summer Showdown with the Star Maker. He keeps it through August 2008, beating Brent Hill and Wolf Hawkins in a three-way match at Hotter Than Hell. He is still champion at the end of September 2008; at Destructive Energy, in a three-way match with Johnny Bloodstone and Tommy Cornell, he and Bloodstone together make Cornell submit, and Mayhem Midden says he must take the result to the Board. He keeps it through October 2008, carrying a new custom belt as the Standing Champion, beating Sammy Bach & Wolf Hawkins with Koshiro Ino and drawing with Sam Keith against Jeremy Stone & Tommy Cornell; at Crunch Time he beats Jeremy Stone and Remo Richardson in a three-way match with the Star Maker. He keeps it through November 2008: on Total Wrestling in the first week the Board's edict recognises his belt and Johnny Bloodstone's and orders the two unified at Malice in Wonderland in January; he beats Jeremy Stone with the Star Maker, beats Tommy Cornell & Tyson Baine with Rick Law and loses a six-man match with John Anderson and Johnny Bloodstone to Chris Rockwell, Tommy Cornell & Wolf Hawkins; at A Little South Of Sanity, with the belt not at stake, he beats Tommy Cornell with the Star Maker. He keeps it through December 2008, drawing with Eric Tyler in twenty minutes, fighting Tommy Cornell to a no contest when Jack Bruce returns and, at Psycho Circus, beating Eddie Peak and Jeremy Stone in a three-way match with the Star Maker after Cornell has attacked him and Peak with the retired TCW belt.

title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-international-championship
label: Koshiro Ino

won.source: Total Mayhem 13, Sunday Week 4 May 2008 (in-game): 'Koshiro Ino defeated Wolf Hawkins for the International Championship'.

how: Won from Wolf Hawkins in a no-disqualification match at Total Mayhem 13 with the Kobra's Bite. He keeps it through June 2008: he beats Sam Keith on Total Wrestling in Week 2, and at Excessive Force he loses to Chris Rockwell by disqualification, which the diary's next preview (p249) treats as no change, billing Ino as champion. He keeps it through July 2008: the diary's result line has Tommy Cornell beating him on Total Wrestling by disqualification after Sam Keith's chairshot, which leaves the title with Ino (the next preview bills him as champion), and at Summer Showdown he beats Sammy Bach with the Kobra's Bite. He loses it to John Anderson at Hotter Than Hell in August 2008, when Anderson boots him in the gut and lands the Ammo Dump onto his injured head.

title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-international-championship
label: John Anderson

won.source: Hotter Than Hell, Sunday Week 4 August 2008 (in-game): 'John Anderson defeated Koshiro Ino', 'giving TCW a new International Championship'.

how: Won from Koshiro Ino at Hotter Than Hell with the Ammo Dump onto Ino's injured head, after Ino's head hit the ringpost, Ino taking too long to cover after Wolf Hawkins hit Anderson with the Full Moon Rising on his behalf; the diary calls it 'a new International Championship', and the Syndicate's Tommy Cornell growls that Anderson remembered how to wrestle once they let him go. He keeps it through September 2008, beaten only by count out by Wolf Hawkins, then beating Frankie Perez, Acid and, at Destructive Energy, Eric Tyler with the Ammo Dump. He keeps it through October 2008, drawing with Sean Deeley and beating Jack Marlowe with the Ammo Dump; at Crunch Time, answering his own open challenge, he is beaten by Deeley by count-out, which the diary does not treat as a title change. He keeps it through November 2008, beating Texas Pete with the Ammo Dump after Wolf Hawkins' interference; at A Little South Of Sanity he beats Pete and Hawkins in a three-way match, pinning Hawkins with the Ammo Dump. He keeps it through December 2008, beating American Buffalo with the Ammo Dump, drawing with Wolf Hawkins at the time limit and, at Psycho Circus, beating Hawkins clean with the Ammo Dump after fifteen minutes.

title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-all-action-championship
label: Edd Stone

won.source: Total Mayhem 13, Sunday Week 4 May 2008 (in-game): 'Edd Stone defeated Sammy Bach for the All Action Championship'.

how: Won from Sammy Bach at Total Mayhem 13 with a top-rope Party's Over, the Syndicate's fourth belt. He defends it at Excessive Force in June 2008 in the Hangtime Match of his own devising, against Sammy Bach and Acid, and keeps it. He keeps it through July 2008, beating Hell Monkey at Summer Showdown with the Party's Over. He keeps it through August 2008: Art Reed, the fans' choice, beats him at Hotter Than Hell only by count out. He keeps it through September 2008, beating the Cannonball Kid on Badge of Honor and Art Reed again at Destructive Energy. He loses it to Frankie Perez at Crunch Time in October 2008, when Perez catches him with a mule kick to the head and applies the P-Clutch.

title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-all-action-championship
label: Frankie Perez

won.source: Crunch Time, Sunday Week 4 October 2008 (in-game): 'Frankie Perez defeated Edd Stone'.

how: Won from Edd Stone at Crunch Time with the P-Clutch, after a mule kick to the head sends Stone spinning and Perez drags him back to the centre of the ring by the hair; the diary calls it his first TCW gold, won in around nine months with the company. He keeps it through November 2008, losing a non-title match to Rick Law on Badge of Honor; at A Little South Of Sanity, in his first defence, he beats Art Reed, Greg Keith and Freddy Huggins, working over Keith's injured arm and clamping on the P-Clutch for the submission. He keeps it through December 2008: at Psycho Circus, with Phil Vibert at his side, he beats Hell Monkey with the P-Clutch after Hell Monkey's Tumbling Monkey misses.

title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-tag-team-championship
label: The Machines

won.source: The diary's Total Mayhem 13 preview (Sunday Week 4 May 2008) calls the title 'now celebrating a full year in the possession of the Machines', and Troy Tornado tells the Young Guns 'The Machines? They won those belts a year ago'; the month is that year back from May 2008.

how: Champions when the diary opens; retain against Painful Procedure at Where Angels Fear To Tread and against the Young Guns at Total Mayhem 13. They lose the belts to the New Wave at Excessive Force in June 2008.

title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-world-heavyweight-championship
label: Johnny Bloodstone

won.source: Crunch Time prediction key, Sunday Week 4 October 2008 (in-game): 'TCW World Heavyweight Championship (Canadian Belt)* Johnny Bloodstone (c)'; his claim comes from Destructive Energy in September 2008, and the diary shows the Board recognising his belt on Total Wrestling in the first week of November 2008.

how: Holder of the second World Heavyweight Championship belt the diary shows from October 2008, the Canadian Belt, after he and Troy Tornado together made Tommy Cornell submit at Destructive Energy and the Board left both men with a claim; the prediction key bills him '(c)'. He keeps it at Crunch Time, beating Brent Hill with the Bloodstone Mutilation, and the diary says the belts will be reunited sooner or later. He keeps it through November 2008: on Total Wrestling in the first week the Board's edict recognises his belt and Troy Tornado's and orders the two unified at Malice in Wonderland in January; he beats Sean Deeley on Badge of Honor, beats the Elite Express with Sam Keith and loses a six-man match with John Anderson and Troy Tornado to Chris Rockwell, Tommy Cornell & Wolf Hawkins; at A Little South Of Sanity he beats Chris Rockwell after half an hour, pinning him in an improvised pin attempt. He keeps it through December 2008, beating Edd Stone with the Bloodstone Mutilation on Total Wrestling and Merle O'Curle in a non-title match on Badge of Honor; the diary's Psycho Circus preview treats the match that decides who faces him at Malice in Wonderland as a title unification match.

title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-tag-team-championship
label: The New Wave

won.source: Excessive Force, Sunday Week 4 June 2008 (in-game): 'The New Wave defeated The Machines'.

how: Won from the Machines at Excessive Force when Scout made John Anderson submit to the Special Force, with the Young Guns at ringside to stop Syndicate backup: Troy Tornado had put the New Wave in the Young Guns' place for the match in return for the Young Guns' first shot at the belts after they won them. They keep the belts through July 2008, beating the Young Guns at Summer Showdown with the Special Force. They keep the belts through August 2008, beating the Easy Riders and the British Lions on television and the School of Tradition at Hotter Than Hell. They keep the belts through September 2008, beating the Keith Brothers, the Enforcers and, at Destructive Energy, the School of Tradition. They keep the belts through October 2008, drawing with the Stone Brothers and beating Acid Dragon and the British Lions; at Crunch Time they beat the Easy Riders only by disqualification. They keep the belts through November 2008, beating the Elite Express, the British Lions and, in non-title matches, American Buffalo & JD Morgan, and going to a no contest with the Keith Brothers; at A Little South Of Sanity they beat the Easy Riders and the Stone Brothers in a three-team elimination match, Scout's Special Force finishing the Stones. They lose the belts to the Easy Riders at Psycho Circus in December 2008 in a hardcore match, Scout choked against the turnbuckle with a chain and Guide finished with the Emergency Stop onto a steel chair.

title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-hard-hitting-championship
label: Sam Keith

won.source: Excessive Force, Sunday Week 4 June 2008 (in-game): 'Sam Keith defeated Eddie Peak, Ricky Dale Johnson, and Tyson Baine'.

how: The first champion: won the four-way No Holds Barred match at Excessive Force over Eddie Peak, Ricky Dale Johnson and Tyson Baine, thumbing Baine in the eye, kicking him low and making him tap to the Proton Lock with the ropes for leverage. He keeps it through July 2008, winning by disqualification over Tyson Baine on Total Wrestling and beating Ricky Dale Johnson at Summer Showdown with the Proton Lock. He keeps it through August 2008, beating Sammy Bach on Total Wrestling and Tommy Cornell in a No Holds Barred match at Hotter Than Hell with the Proton Lock. He keeps it through September 2008, drawing with Chris Rockwell on Total Wrestling and beating Jeremy Stone in a No Holds Barred match at Destructive Energy with the Proton Lock. He keeps it through November 2008, beating JD Morgan with the Proton Lock and being hit with a chair by Sammy Bach; at A Little South Of Sanity he beats Bach with the NeutronPlex. He keeps it through December 2008: at Psycho Circus, in a No Holds Barred match with Sammy Bach, he is not beaten; Bach wins by disqualification when Texas Pete hits him with a chair, which the diary does not treat as a title change.

title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-international-championship
label: Wolf Hawkins

won.source: The diary's roster entry of 18 February 2008 calls him 'Currently the International champion'; it does not date his win.

how: Champion when the diary opens; keeps it at Where Angels Fear To Tread through Sam Keith's interference and loses it to Koshiro Ino at Total Mayhem 13.
note: At Where Angels Fear To Tread the diary's result line reads 'Koshiro Ino defeated Wolf Hawkins', but its match report has Hawkins pinning Ino and keeping the title, and the May shows bill Hawkins as champion until Total Mayhem 13.

title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-all-action-championship
label: Sammy Bach

won.source: The diary's roster entry of 20 February 2008 calls him 'a champion, the All-Action guy'; it does not date his win.

how: Champion when the diary opens; keeps it against Johnny Bloodstone at Where Angels Fear To Tread (a disqualification) and loses it to Edd Stone at Total Mayhem 13.

title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-world-heavyweight-championship
label: Tommy Cornell

won.source: The diary's roster entry of 18 February 2008 calls him 'the champ'; its Total Mayhem 13 preview (Sunday Week 4 May 2008) says he 'has held his title for an amazing seventeen months', and Troy Tornado's promo on Tuesday Week 2 April 2008 says 'Fifteen months is plenty of time to have it'. The diary does not date the win.

how: Champion when the diary opens, and still champion after Total Mayhem 13, where Troy Tornado wins by disqualification; the diary puts his win about seventeen months before May 2008 in one place and fifteen months before April 2008 in another, and dates it nowhere. He loses it to Troy Tornado at Excessive Force in June 2008, when Tornado catches him coming off the top rope with the Star Maker.

title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-tag-team-championship
label: The Easy Riders

won.source: Psycho Circus, Sunday Week 4 December 2008 (in-game): 'Easy Riders defeated the New Wave'.

how: Won from the New Wave at Psycho Circus in a hardcore match, Billy Fonda and Peter Hopper beating down Scout, anchoring him to the turnbuckle with a chain that Carl Batch holds round his neck, and finishing Guide with the Emergency Stop onto a steel chair; the diary notes that the New Wave's long reign has ended and that it is not sure the Easy Riders will endure as long.
